title: High Strength and Fracture Resistance of Reduced-Activity W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr High-Entropy Alloy for Fusion Energy Applications.

recollection.starting_material: Elemental powders or ingots of W, Ta, Ti, V and Zr mixed in near-equiatomic ratios to form a high-entropy alloy
recollection.intervention: Vacuum arc melting or powder metallurgy followed by homogenisation and possibly thermo-mechanical processing/annealing to obtain a reduced-radioactivity HEA
recollection.structure: A single-phase body-centred cubic (BCC) solid solution, possibly with nanometre-scale B2- or Laves-type precipitates dispersed in the matrix
recollection.mechanism: Solid-solution lattice-distortion strengthening from the five refractory elements, combined with precipitation and grain-boundary strengthening, giving good high-temperature strength and crack-tip blunting for high fracture toughness
recollection.results: Likely room-temperature yield strength above 1.2–1.5 GPa, tensile ductility of ~10–15 %, and fracture toughness on the order of 70–100 MPa·m^0.5; strength retention above 800 °C suitable for fusion first-wall applications

score.note: Partially recalls arc melting and near-equiatomic elemental feedstock, but invents homogenization/thermomechanical processing and omits the measured comparisons. The single-phase/precipitate structure is wrong; the alloy had segregated W-Ta-rich and Zr-Ti-rich regions forming two BCC phases. Solid-solution and lattice-distortion strengthening are correct, but precipitation and grain-boundary strengthening were not established. The estimated yield strength is fairly close to ~1.6 GPa, while ductility, toughness (actual ~38 MPa√m), and claimed >800 °C performance are incorrect.
